instruction:
GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Revit graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, Dynamo, pyRevit, macros, external API automation, Python, or any helper script/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only Revit native GUI tools, menus, dialogs, schedules, sheets, and built-in export commands. Start from a blank Revit project. Using the Revit GUI, create a single-storey cafe pavilion with an overall rectangular footprint of 16.0 m by 10.0 m near the project origin. The exterior walls should rise about 3.4 m, with one ground slab, a roof covering the footprint, and a curtain-glazed front facade along the 16.0 m side. Save the deliverables on the Desktop using the exact filenames required below.

The IFC export must use the IFC4 schema, have unique GlobalId values for all IfcRoot objects, and contain one IfcProject, one IfcSite, one IfcBuilding, one IfcBuildingStorey, four IfcSpace entities, six IfcWall entities, one IfcSlab, one IfcRoof, three IfcDoor entities, six IfcWindow entities, and one IfcCurtainWall. Do not include IfcStair, IfcColumn, IfcBeam, or IfcBuildingElementProxy entities. Name the spaces so the normalized IfcSpace names include Cafe, Storage, Prep, and Toilet. Export a facade opening/count schedule named result.csv with headers type,count and exactly these rows: front curtain glazing=4, east side windows=2, and entry glazed door=1. The required BIM categories must be exported as real IFC building elements/spaces, not visual-only placeholders or proxy geometry. Coordinate placement, relationship entities, GUID values, Revit type names, materials, property sets, and harmless extra metadata may vary as long as the stated model geometry, element categories, space names, schedules, sheets, and file outputs are satisfied.
